_comment: Source of truth for the README boards section. TWO lists, deliberately: 'boards' is the SUPPORTED table — only keyboards Aether can actually drive, i.e. exactly the registry entries with offerInUi true (data/board_registry.json). 'recognized' is the identify-only list — boards Aether detects, names and draws but cannot drive, kept visible so the app can explain itself instead of silently pretending a board doesn't exist. Every entry carries the registry `slug` that ties it to data/board_registry.json; tests/test_boards.py fails if the two files drift apart. After editing, run `python tools/gen_boards_table.py --write` (CI checks the README stays in sync). Fields: slug, name, switches, lighting/actuation = true|false|"wip", status. Cell semantics differ from the registry's capability flags ON PURPOSE: the registry records whether a command is wired, this table records what a USER can rely on — so a board whose protocol is shared-by-inference but never round-tripped on the physical hardware shows "wip", not a tick.
